## Publish gate report

**Going out:** landing hero copy, brand site, UK audience. Publish time not given.

**Claims check**
| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "you'll love it or it's free" | **Fails.** Policy section 3 bans "you'll love it or it's free" because we have no such offer. It is a guarantee. |
| "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time" | OK. Matches the policy row (subscription terms). |
| "free UK delivery on orders over £25" | OK. Matches the policy row (shipping policy). |
| "means most boxes ship free" | **Unproven.** No order-value data is on file, so we can't say most boxes clear £25. It also implies a statistic. Remove it. |

**Regulated claims:** the guarantee and the free-delivery line are the only offer-type claims. The guarantee is the problem above. Nothing on health, environment or children.

**House style:** voice is warm and plain, and no banned words appear. Score about 85 once the guarantee is gone. No AI tells.

**Disclosure:** none needed. This is our own site copy, not a paid partnership, affiliate link or gifted product.

**Fixed (suggested rewrite, not yet approved):**
> Tea that's easy to stop and start. Subscribers can pause or cancel any time, and UK delivery is free on orders over £25.

- Removed "you'll love it or it's free".
- Removed "means most boxes ship free". The delivery line now uses the policy wording.

**Needs a decision:** if the team wants a satisfaction guarantee or a "most orders ship free" line, it needs a real offer or data added to the policy first. I'd leave both out.

**Approver:** Sam (marketing lead). Nothing goes live until Sam gives an explicit yes to the exact rewritten copy above. The original draft should not be published.
